name: s2-ecology-to-proximity
title: S2 — Ecology to proximity: when does cross-feeding select for persistent contact?
concept: Physical association made operational as encounter rate, adhesion lifetime, diffusion length, and spatial crowding. Two metabolic agents (the S1 pair) embedded in a reaction-diffusion environment; vary diffusion, flow, adhesion, crowding, and partner density.
question: When do cross-feeding benefits select for persistent proximity rather than independent coexistence? Does the predicted selection for proximity disappear under high diffusion / well-mixed conditions?
hypothesis: Below a critical diffusion length the cross-feeding fitness advantage is distance-dependent and selects for sustained contact; under well-mixed (high-diffusion) conditions the proximity advantage collapses, so selection for contact is a spatial-structure effect, not a given.
claim: Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (finite-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding advantage is distance-dependent and favors persistent proximity, creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis — but the advantage vanishes under high diffusion / well-mixed conditions, so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.

behavior_tests.name: proximity-selected-under-finite-diffusion
behavior_tests.description: Fitness advantage increases as inter-partner separation decreases (finite diffusion).

provenance.note: Slope of fitness vs -separation (normalized); >0.1 = a measurable distance-dependent advantage. Calibrate against S2 parameter priors from Radler-2026 protrusion length scales.

behavior_tests.name: advantage-vanishes-well-mixed
behavior_tests.description: The proximity advantage collapses under high diffusion (well-mixed control).

literature_anchors.expectation: Asgard protrusions set the length/time scales of transient contact.
